paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter teaches me. Sin shows up before the worst thing does. The LORD told Cain, "sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it" (Genesis 4:7). He said it while Cain was only angry, before anybody got hurt, and that is the moment to listen.

Now look at what Cain does with his answer. He says, "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Genesis 4:9). Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain acts like keeping his own brother is a bridge too far. Anger, hiding and excuses, they all pile up fast, and the LORD still asked Cain a question first, "Where is your brother Abel?"

Then comes the part that gets me. Even after all that, the LORD put a mark on Cain so no one who found him would kill him (Genesis 4:15). Lamech goes the other way and brags about seventy-sevenfold (Genesis 4:24). And at the very end, men "began to call upon the name of the LORD" (Genesis 4:26). So when sin is crouching at YOUR door, baker, don't hide and don't make excuses. Call on the LORD.
